title: Same $100, 4 Friends: One Made $660... or Owes $144 #shorts
description:
Four friends get the same $100 for one year. 1 keeps it in a jar. 2 buys 4 hens. 3 buys a new hen whenever he can. 4 borrows $400 and buys 20 hens.

Good year: $100 (worth $96 after inflation), $222, $293, $660.
Bird flu in June (the whole flock is culled): $100, $61, $21, and friend 4 still owes $144.

Borrowing multiplies wins AND losses. That's the part most versions of this famous parable leave out.

Story math (simplified on purpose): a hen costs $25, lays 20 dozen eggs a year and eats $15 of feed a year; eggs sell at the US average price, $2.27 a dozen (BLS, September 2026; it averaged $4.25 in 2025 during the bird-flu shortage); friend 4's loan is $400 at 12% a year. No taxes, labour or housing costs. Inflation: US CPI, last 12 months (4.0%). When bird flu is found on a farm, the flock is culled (USDA APHIS).

Which friend are you? Comment 1, 2, 3 or 4.

This is a teaching story, not financial advice. Leverage can lose more than you put in.
Original script and animation, inspired by a classic money parable. Narrated with an AI voice.
